source: canvas.json of the published design canvas, version 26: the stickies of its Range section

range-intro.text:
Range direction (Hairline-inspired)

The owner, in their words: "We need to convince people we can do ANYTHING ... The portfolio page will be our proof of that." And on Hairline UI: "hairline ui is actually not bad, especially their light-dark transition".

What we take from Hairline: a big headline whose accent word swaps with the picked category; category tabs sitting on a peek carousel (a centre plate, dimmed plates either side); light and dark themes that both look finished; a theme switch that spreads out from the toggle; dot fields at the page edges.

Rules relaxed for the portfolio only: motion is welcome (one load moment, the word swap, plate moves, the theme reveal, live motion inside exhibits), each with a reduced-motion fallback and no autoplay. The one-bold-thing rule is lifted. No purple, no gradients, Red Hat type, tokens only.

Accent: one blue, #1F4FD1 in light (5.6:1 on the grey, 6.8:1 on white) and #7FA2FF in dark (7.4:1 on the page, 6.6:1 on a plate).

sticky-range-light.text:
What it is: the range page in the light theme, with the phone version beside it. The headline reads "We build dashboards. We break them first." The blue word follows the tab: dashboards, finance apps, mobile apps, AI features, 3D scenes, websites, test suites. Seven tabs sit on the peek carousel, one plate each, opening on Dashboards so Central Command is the first thing people see: Dashboards (Central Command), Finance (Tally & Trace), Mobile, AI features and 3D & motion (lab demos with a dashed "Lab demo" tag), Sites (this site), and Testing (this site's Playwright suite, with ticks that land one by one). Try it: tick habits in the phone app, press Draft a reply, pause the cube, sort the bills.

Motion: on first load the two headline lines rise, the dots fade in and the stage slides up, about 0.9s in all and played once. Picking a tab swaps the word and slides the plate in from the side it came from. The moon button switches theme: in a browser with View Transitions it is a circular reveal spreading from the button (about 0.55s); under reduced motion, or without View Transitions, it swaps at once. The canvas runtime may not show the reveal; the toggle still switches the theme.

How it differs from Hairline: our gallery grey, not white; one blue rather than blue and purple; the dots are a fixed ordered dither in the accent, not a coloured field; plates are real working fragments, not screenshots; every plate says who checked it.

Phone: one centred axis with 16px gutters. The logo sits centred between the theme toggle and Menu; headline, intro and plate headings are centred, the two buttons stack full width. The categories are one sideways-scrolling chip row between two matching scroll buttons, and a picked chip scrolls to the middle. Tables and lists inside fragments stay left-aligned. One plate at a time, with back and next buttons centred under it.

Open choices: the headline line ("We break them first." or "We build it. We break it."); whether lab demos belong on the home page or only on /lab; the 3D demo: the owner settled on the CSS cube for now (three.js, about 150KB, is not planned); the tab list itself; whether the phone chips should wrap into centred lines instead of scrolling.

The people (owner, for recruiters: two individuals open for hire, not just a dev shop): the nav is Work, Seth, Christine, Writing, with Start a project as the client button. Each real-project plate carries one credit line, "Built by Seth · Tested by Christine", linking to the person panels. "The two of us" sits between the carousel and Every project: one frame split by an ink rule (a pair, not a card grid; stacked on the phone). Each half has a real photo cropped to the face, the name, the role and a fact line, a two-sentence pitch, Open to (Full-time · Contract · Remote or relocation), "What I did here" from the real projects only, Download CV (PDF), Email, LinkedIn and GitHub. Under it: "Or hire us both for your project or idea". The contact section is for clients only and points recruiters to Seth or Christine directly. Real details now: Seth Palileo, Lead Software Engineer (10+ years shipping production systems), seth@studiosc.dev, GitHub smpalileo; Christine Nacar-Palileo, Senior QA Engineer (11+ years building test automation), christine@studiosc.dev, GitHub cdtncr. The photos are real, from the owner, re-saved without EXIF, XMP or location data and resized to 1200px.

Holly, Chief Morale Officer: a small section after The two of us, before Every project. Her photos sit in a small pile of prints with a soft 2.5rem radius (unlike the people photos, since she is not staff): the current one on top, the next two peeking out behind it at 4° and −3°, hairline frames, no shadows. Previous and next buttons and a "1 / 6" counter (announced politely) flip through them, and so do the left and right arrow keys when the pile has focus. Moving on slides the top print out and tucks it to the back in 300 ms while the rest settle; going back pulls the bottom print out to the top. Under reduced motion the order just changes. The order is collar, chair, garden, nose, side-eye, upside-down, then back to the collar. On the phone the intent is to swipe the pile as well, but the buttons are there too and are what is drawn; the heading Holly with Chief Morale Officer under it (the word "And" sits in the gap after "Or hire us both for your project or idea", in the display face at the heading's size and on its left edge, so it reads "And / Holly" across the gap; centred on the phone), the owner's copy in one paragraph (the owner is still choosing between variations, so it is one edit to swap), Breed (Pembroke Welsh Corgi) and Age. Age is worked out at render from her birthday, 31 July 2023, to two decimals ("3.31 years old" today); it has no timer and no motion, and hovering it shows "Born 31 July 2023". The line drawing is a Pembroke Welsh Corgi: long low body on short legs, deep chest, round rear with no tail, big upright pointed ears and a fox-like muzzle. Above the button: "Very flexible rates: anything beef or duck will do." Give Holly a treat adds to Treats today (announced politely) moves the pile on one print, and gives one corgi wiggle of the rear (360 ms) with an ear twitch (300 ms), only on a click and never under reduced motion. The count lives on the page only; a shared count across all visitors would need a tiny free-tier store and is an option. Suggested, not drawn: a 404 page that says "Holly ate this page" with a link home.

The three of us: right after Holly's section, before Writing, the wide photo of all three on the sofa sits on its own as a pause, full width of the page column (2:1 on desktop, 3:2 on the phone), captioned "Sprint planning. Holly abstained."

Writing: after that photo and before Every project, two large links side by side (stacked on the phone), not cards and with no counts: "How we build" (technical posts, /blog/work, "Notes from the projects on this page") and "Off the clock" (everything else, /blog/life, "Trips, food, Holly, and whatever we got up to lately"). /blog/work and /blog/life are new filtered views of the blog, so every post needs a category (work or life) in its front matter.

sticky-range-dark.text:
What it is: the same page in the dark theme, drawn as the settled state, so there is no load motion on this board. The dark grey is #141619, plates #1D2024, body text #ECEEF1 (15.6:1), muted text #A3A9B2 (7.7:1), accent #7FA2FF (7.4:1). The working fragments (bills table, day feed, route checks) keep their own light palettes on purpose: each product looks the way it really ships.

How it differs from Hairline: a neutral graphite with no navy or purple tint, and the same single blue made lighter, rather than a second palette.

Open choices: follow the system setting on first visit or always open light; whether light-palette fragments on dark plates feel right or each product needs a dark version (more build work for every fragment).

The people section and plate credits are mirrored here from the light board; the person frame uses the plate colour with an ink rule, so it reads in both themes.

sticky-range-profile.text:
What it is: Seth's own page at /seth, which the nav and his person panel link to. Header with Seth marked as the current page; large name, role (Lead Software Engineer), the CV headline line "AI Automation Lead (LLM Integration, Workflow Automation, TechOps)" and the fact line (10+ years shipping production systems); his photo; the pitch and the Open to row; Download CV, Email Seth (seth@studiosc.dev), LinkedIn and GitHub (smpalileo). Selected work is the three real projects from the plates, plus the 18 November reconciliation post. Client work follows in the same list style: Space Reserve, PSJ, Entame Choice and BIS (which replaces Pouch), each with the role Lead engineer and solutions architect and its stack from the CV. They are not under NDA; there are no status tags, no repo links and no outbound links. Highlights are three short rows from the CV (First Mate Technologies, Asurion, SiteMinder), a muted line for the earlier roles from 2016 and the education line. Then a Photos gallery (see the gallery sticky). Skills use the six groups from the updated CV, with recent studio work layered in. Above the closing line, a small photo of Seth with Holly, captioned "With Holly, off the clock". It closes on a line pointing to Christine's page. The photos are real, from the owner, re-saved without EXIF, XMP or location data and resized to 1200px. The theme toggle works.

Open choice: whether the CV PDF lives at /cv/seth.pdf.

sticky-seth-skills.text:
Seth's skills: the six groups from the updated CV (AI & LLMs; Automation & Workflows; TechOps & Infrastructure; Engineering; Security & Governance; Project Leadership) are the base. Added on top (please check):

• AI & LLMs: "a multi-model audit harness where Claude, Codex and DeepSeek independently review every plan and pull request, model routing by cost and risk".
• Automation & Workflows: "including Trailhead, a self-built pipeline that turns tickets into reviewed pull requests", "Playwright UI verification judged by AI verifiers" and "artifact-driven development with a clickable mock-up before every feature".
• TechOps & Infrastructure: Cloudflare (Workers, D1, KV), Vercel, Render, Supabase and "a self-hosted Docker Compose stack behind Traefik".
• Engineering: Vue.js, Tailwind and Stripe (kept from the old CV), plus React Native and Expo, Prisma, Drizzle, Turborepo and pnpm monorepos.
• Security & Governance: "security headers and a content security policy, rate limiting, rotating refresh tokens in httpOnly cookies" (from published posts).

Project Leadership is the CV text as is.

sticky-profile-gallery.text:
Owner will supply photos and captions.

Both profile pages, desktop and phone, now have a Photos gallery before Skills. It works like the life-post gallery: one photo at a time with its caption and n / N, back and next that wrap, thumbnails, and a 200ms crossfade (instant under reduced motion). Stand-ins for now: Seth's page uses seth, seth-holly, holly-collar and holly-chair; Christine's uses christine, christine-holly, christine-alt and holly-garden. The photo of the three of us stays on home only. Captions are [PLACEHOLDER]; each photo keeps a descriptive alt.

sticky-range-profile-christine.text: What it is: Christine's page at /christine, the same layout as Seth's. Header with Christine as the current page; Christine Nacar-Palileo, Senior QA Engineer, 11+ years building test automation; her photo; her pitch and the Open to row; Download CV (/cv/christine.pdf), Email Christine (christine@studiosc.dev), LinkedIn and GitHub (cdtncr). Selected work is her testing on the three real projects, from the plates. Highlights are three short rows from her CV (SiteMinder, RedPoint Global, Betica Technology Solutions), a muted line for the earlier roles from 2012 and the education line. Then the same Photos gallery as Seth's page. Skills follow the six CV groups plus Studio QA. Above the closing line, a small photo of her with Holly, captioned "With Holly, off the clock". It closes on a line pointing back to Seth's page. The photos are real, from the owner, re-saved without EXIF, XMP or location data and resized to 1200px.

sticky-christine-skills.text:
Christine's skills, regrouped into the six CV groups plus one new group. New lines (copy we wrote, please check):

• AI Tools: Copilot, Claude, Gemini, Glean, plus "AI-assisted QA, with AI verifiers judging Playwright screenshots against acceptance criteria".
• Languages & APIs: added REST.
• CI/CD: Buildkite, Git, plus "release QA on Vercel, Render and Cloudflare deploys".
• Testing Utilities: added Puppeteer.
• Databases (new group): SQL Server, MongoDB, plus "Supabase and Postgres data QA".
• Studio QA (new group): "Acceptance-criteria and scenario-test design for every StudioSC app, visual regression and mock-up fidelity checks, Lighthouse performance budgets, accessibility testing with axe, mobile app QA on Expo, Linear workflow".

Automation Frameworks is unchanged from the CV.
